# Running an Alchemy 2 stack locally with Vite

verified: 2026-11-02

Answers how kurasu's stack runs under `alchemy dev` with Vite in front: which ports it uses, how Vite's proxy learns the API Worker's URL, how the classroom WebSocket reaches the API Worker, when the Worker's construction runs, what a Durable Object binding is called and what shape drizzle-kit gives the migrations. The facts come from kurasu's implementation on alchemy 2.0.0 beta.

## Knowledge

- The API Worker declares `dev: { port: 1337 }`, and when 1337 is taken (by another stack, for example) it starts on the next free port, so its real URL is `api.url` in the stack. Vite's proxy forwards `/api` to that URL with `ws: true`, so the browser sees a single origin as in production.
- `Website.Vite` passes the dev server only the `VITE_` entries of its `env`, as `import.meta.env.VITE_*` `define`s in Vite's inline config; the Vite process does not get the Worker's other env entries or any per-Worker process variable. The stack gives the web `env: { VITE_API_URL: api.url }` in dev only, and a dev-only plugin in `apps/web/vite.config.ts` (`apiProxy`) reads `config.define["import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL"]` in its `config` hook and sets the proxy target. This works because Vite merges the inline config into the config file's before it runs the plugins' `config` hooks. The value stays out of the deployed web: the build only inlines `VITE_` keys that the props carry, and the production props have none.
- Under `alchemy dev`, `Website.Vite` injects the Cloudflare plugin. That plugin sends every WebSocket upgrade except Vite's HMR to the web's Worker, and the web's Worker answers `/api/classroom` with the SPA's 404 before the proxy gets the request. A dev-only Vite plugin (`apiUpgradesToProxy` in `apps/web/vite.config.ts`, `apply: "serve"`) hands `/api/` upgrades to the proxy's listener only. It relies on Vite registering the proxy's upgrade listener after the `configureServer` hooks and before their post callbacks, so the proxy's listener is the last one when the plugin's post callback runs.
- A Worker's construction (the `Effect.gen` passed to `Cloudflare.Worker`) runs at plan time as well as when the isolate starts, and the bindings exist only in the second. Anything that reads a binding, such as the layers that query D1, is built inside `fetch`.
- A Durable Object binding takes the Durable Object's name, `Aula` in kurasu, which is also its class name. There is no separate binding name such as `AULA`.
- drizzle-kit 1.0 generates each migration as a folder holding `migration.sql` and `snapshot.json` (`migrations/0001_users_and_codes/`), not as a loose `.sql` file. The D1 resource takes the `migrations` folder and applies them.
- drizzle-kit writes a text primary key as `` `id` text PRIMARY KEY `` and ignores `.notNull()` on it, and SQLite lets a text primary key hold NULL. Every table's `id` in kurasu is `NOT NULL`, written by hand in the migration that creates or rebuilds the table; `drizzle-kit generate` still reports no schema changes afterwards. A migration that drizzle-kit generates and that rebuilds a table loses the `NOT NULL`, so add it back by hand. D1 always enforces foreign keys, and `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` does nothing in a migration; a rebuild uses `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = on`, and a table that other tables reference is rebuilt by copying its rows aside, dropping it, creating it again and copying them back, because dropping it and renaming a new table leaves the child rows as violations at commit.
- The web origin used in links differs per stage: `KURASU_WEB_ORIGIN` is computed in `.env.schema` as `http://localhost:5173` in dev and `https://<domain>` in production, so a link mailed from the local stack opens the local web.

# agent-browser

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP with accessibility-tree snapshots and compact `@eN` element refs.

Install: `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`

## Start here

This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide. Before running any `agent-browser` command, load the actual workflow content from the CLI:

```bash
agent-browser skills get core             # start here — workflows, common patterns, troubleshooting
agent-browser skills get core --full      # include full command reference and templates
```

The CLI serves skill content that always matches the installed version, so instructions never go stale. The content in this stub cannot change between releases, which is why it just points at `skills get core`.

## Visible browser inside herdr

Render the browser in a herdr pane so the user can watch it. Run these in order.

Resolve the `official.browser` plugin root and substitute the printed path literally into the `bun run` commands below. Read it from the CLI rather than hardcoding it, because the directory name carries a content hash that changes when the plugin updates. A shell variable does not survive between commands, so do not try to carry it in one:

```bash
herdr plugin list --plugin official.browser --json | jq -r '.result.plugins[0].plugin_root'
```

Open the pane and keep `pane_id` from the response (`--placement` also takes `tab`, `zoomed`, `overlay`):

```bash
herdr plugin pane open --plugin official.browser --entrypoint browser --placement split --direction right --no-focus
```

List the views and pick the one whose `pane_id` matches. Never guess when several are listed:

```bash
bun run <plugin_root>/src/cli.ts views
```

Attach to that view, then pass `--session herdr` on every later command. Re-running `connect` returns the same endpoint:

```bash
bun run <plugin_root>/src/cli.ts connect --view <view_id>
agent-browser connect <cdp_http_url> --session herdr
```

When done, detach before closing the pane:

```bash
agent-browser --session herdr close
herdr plugin pane close <pane_id>
```

If a `herdr` command reports `protocol_mismatch`, the running server is older than the installed CLI. Tell the user and stop — restarting the server kills every pane process, including this session, so it is their call.

Load mahou:basics first. Then read `.mahou/commit-changes.md` if present.

# Commit changes

Commits the changes done to this repository using conventional commits (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/). This is the one skill whose job is committing, so the user asking for it, or a skill reaching a commit step the user approved, is the consent `basics` asks for. Pushing is not part of the job.

## Message format

```
<type>[optional scope]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

Types:

- **fix**: patches a bug (PATCH in semantic versioning)
- **feat**: introduces a feature (MINOR)
- A `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer marks a breaking change (MAJOR) and can go on a commit of any type. Never use the `!` after the type or scope for this.
- **build**, **chore**, **ci**, **docs**, **style**, **refactor**, **perf**, **test**, with their usual meanings from `@commitlint/config-conventional`.

Footers other than `BREAKING CHANGE: <description>` follow the git trailer format.

## Procedure

1. **Analyze the repository state.** `git status` for everything modified, added and deleted; `git diff` for the nature of each change; `git diff --staged` for anything already staged. When the project has a `CLAUDE.md` or a `.mahou/commit-changes.md` that names a scope convention or a commit convention of its own, read it and follow it.

2. **Plan the groups.** Group by logical relationship: same feature, same fix, same area. Tests, type definitions and directly related changes go with the main change. Never mix unrelated changes in one commit. Refactors go in their own commit unless small and tightly coupled to the main change.

3. **Present the groups and wait.** Always, even when there is one group and it looks obvious. Show every group with its proposed message and its file list, then ask how to proceed: with one group, proceed or split further; with several, proceed or merge. Take the user's regrouping literally.

4. **Commit each approved group.** Stage only that group's files with `git add <file>...`, then commit with the agreed message. Never `git add -A` or `git add .`; an untracked file the user did not mention is not part of any group until they say so.

   A file whose changes belong to two groups is split by hunk. The file appears under both groups with a word on which change goes where. To stage one side, write the file's diff to a temporary patch with `git diff <file> > /tmp/<name>.diff`, delete the hunks that belong to the other group while keeping the diff header, and apply it with `git apply --cached /tmp/<name>.diff`. Once that group is committed, the hunks left in the working tree are what `git add <file>` stages for the other. `git add -p` is interactive and does not run here.

## Message rules

- Description in the imperative, present tense: "add", not "added" or "adding". Short, no trailing period.
- The message says **what** the change does, never why it was made or where the request came from. "fix(auth): add null check for expired tokens", never "fix: address PR comments".
- A body, when needed, is simple and direct: no file listings, no implementation walkthrough, no test section.
- **Scope** is the area of the project the change touches: the top-level module, directory, package or service name, one or two lowercase words. Check `git log` for the scopes the project already uses and reuse them. When the change spans areas, use the primary one; when nothing dominates, omit the scope.

## When something is off

- No changes: say so and stop.
- Merge conflict markers in the tree: say so and stop; nothing is committed over a conflict.
- Untracked files: ask whether they belong in a group before staging them.

Branch `feat/preguntas-en-la-card`: all six decisions are applied and committed in five commits, nothing pushed. `pnpm run check` and `pnpm test` pass.

## Commits
- `3229193` refactor(core): make Write an opaque type that the database adapter wraps and unwraps
- `5597f10` fix(web): read the featured questions switch in dark mode and show a skeleton while the session loads
- `c011391` refactor(web): share the question list and the vote sort between the featured card and the classroom, and skeleton the whole card
- `738e5bc` test(api): move the featuring changelog test to the featured file
- `1a03e01` docs: reconcile the data, classroom, web and prototype docs with the featured session

## What each decision changed
1. **R5, opaque `Write`.**
   - In `packages/core/src/batch.ts`, `Write` is now a branded interface. The core only has a symbol brand and cannot see inside it.
   - `packages/database/src/database.ts` holds one wrap/unwrap pair: `write(statement)` keeps the Drizzle statement in a `WeakMap`, and `batch` unwraps it.
   - `repository.ts` still has its raw `statements` and exposes `writes` through `write`. The one-off statements in `materials`, `users`, `questions` and `sessions` call `write(...)` where they enter a batch.
   - The repo's lint forbids type assertions, so I used the `WeakMap` and no cast. Behaviour is the same.
2. **R12, dark mode.** `FeaturedQuestionsSwitch` uses `border-line` and `text-ink` instead of `border-sand` and `text-coal`. Light mode looks the same, and the title and line read in dark mode.
3. **R7, changelog test.**
   - "featuring a session records nothing" moved to `featured.test.ts`, and the "must run last" comment is gone from `changelog.test.ts`.
   - It needs a session that has no entries and is not featured by another test. I added `sixth` ("Sexta", enabled) to `fixtures/featured.sql`; the test is last in the file and no longer depends on order.
   - `featured.test.ts` and `changelog.test.ts` pass together: 36 tests.
4. **R13 and R17, skeletons.**
   - The switch now shows `SkeletonOf` with `sessionExamples[0]` and has the `skeleton-block` class, so the skeleton has its own size.
   - On the student home, the card did move things: the list skeleton was one placeholder inside a card that already showed its heading and form. I wrapped the whole card in `SkeletonOf` with `questionExamples`.
5. **R1, shared logic.**
   - `useQuestionsByVotes` runs the query and sorts by votes; `StudentQuestionList` holds the rows, vote toggle and delete action.
   - `FeaturedQuestionsCard` is the card body, and `FeaturedQuestions` only picks the skeleton or the card. `StudentQuestions` keeps the form as the list header.
   - `useQuestions` gained a `select` generic for the sort.
   - What each screen shows is unchanged.
6. **Docs draft.** Applied as written: the five docs under `app/docs/`, the `highlighted` to `featured` renames and comments in `inicio-responsive.html` (it draws the same), and the `.mahou/wiki/web.md` line.

## Tests
- Moved: the featuring changelog test, from `changelog.test.ts` to `featured.test.ts`.
- Adjusted in `home-questions.test.tsx`: the "asking from the card…" and "a failed question stays written…" tests now wait for the real card before typing, because the skeleton card now has a copy of the field. They check the same things.
- No new tests. The web suite passes with 287 tests and the API suite with 225 passed and 1 skipped.

## Screenshots
All in `/home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/.scratch/preguntas-en-la-card/reports/decisions/`, taken against the local stack and checked by eye:
- `switch-light.png`
- `switch-dark.png`
- `switch-skeleton.png`
- `home-card-skeleton.png`
- `home-card-loaded.png`

The switch screenshots show a readable switch in both modes and a block of the same size while loading. The home screenshots show the card as one block while loading and then the card with its questions.
